content:
KYC Policy — Know Your Customer
Document: KYC Policy | Version: 1.0 | Department: Retail Banking | Effective: January 2026 | Review: January
2027
1. Purpose
This Know Your Customer (KYC) Policy explains how Riyadh Trust Bank verifies the identity of every customer
before opening an account or providing a banking service. The purpose of KYC is to prevent identity fraud,
money laundering and terrorist financing, and to make sure the bank knows who it is doing business with. Every
employee who opens accounts, updates customer records or reviews customer files must follow this policy. 2. Scope
This policy applies to all individual customers, joint account holders, minors with a guardian, and authorised
representatives acting for a customer. It applies in every branch and through every digital channel of the bank. Corporate customers are covered by a separate Corporate KYC Procedure and are not covered here. 3. Documents Needed for Account Opening
To open a personal account, the customer must provide the following documents. No account may be opened
until all required documents have been received and verified. 3.1 Identity documents
The customer must provide one valid original identity document. For Saudi nationals, this is a valid National ID
card (Hawiya). For residents, this is a valid Iqama (residence permit). The document must not be expired. A
photocopy alone is not accepted; the original must be seen by the branch officer and a certified copy kept on file. 3.2 Proof of address
The customer must provide proof of address dated within the last three months. Accepted proof includes a utility
bill (electricity, water or telephone), a rental contract registered with the landlord, or a national address
certificate. The address on the proof must match the address given on the account opening form. 3.3 Employment and income proof
For a salary account, the customer must provide an employment letter from the employer, or a salary certificate,
showing the employer name, job title and monthly salary. For self-employed customers, a commercial
registration and a recent bank statement of six months are required instead. 3.4 Additional documents for special cases
A guardian opening an account for a minor must provide the minor's birth certificate and the guardian's own
identity document. An authorised representative must provide a valid power of attorney, stamped by a notary,
plus their own identity document. Students must provide a valid student ID from their university or school. 4. Identity Verification Steps
The branch officer must complete the following steps in order. First, check that the identity document is original,
undamaged and not expired. Second, compare the photograph on the document with the person in front of
them. Third, enter the customer details into the core banking system and run the name against the internal
watchlist and the sanctions list. Fourth, verify the proof of address and employment documents. Fifth, record the
verification result and the officer's name in the system. If any step fails, the account must not be opened and the
case must be sent to the Compliance Officer.
title: KYC Policy — Know Your Customer

content:
5. Customer Risk Rating
Every customer is given a risk rating after verification: Low, Medium or High. Most salaried customers with a clear
employment history are Low risk. Customers with complex income sources, frequent large cash deposits or links
to high-risk countries are Medium or High risk. High-risk customers require approval from the Compliance
Officer before the account is opened, and their accounts are reviewed every six months instead of every year. 6. Ongoing Monitoring and Updates
KYC is not a one-time check. Customer information must be updated when the identity document expires, when
the customer changes address or employment, or at least once every three years for Low-risk customers and
once a year for Medium-risk customers. If a customer's documents expire and are not renewed within 30 days,
the account is restricted until the documents are updated. The bank may ask for fresh documents at any time if a
transaction looks unusual. 7. Record Keeping
All KYC documents, verification notes and risk ratings must be kept for at least ten years after the account is
closed. Records must be stored securely, with access limited to authorised staff only. No KYC document may be
shared outside the bank without the written approval of the Compliance Officer. 8. Responsibilities
Branch officers are responsible for collecting and checking documents. The Compliance Officer is responsible for
approving High-risk customers and for training staff. The Branch Manager is responsible for making sure no
account is opened without completed KYC. Any employee who finds a forged document must report it to the
Compliance Officer on the same day. Arabic Summary

Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Policy
Document: AML Policy | Version: 1.0 | Department: Compliance | Effective: January 2026 | Review: July 2026
1. Purpose
This Anti-Money Laundering Policy explains how Riyadh Trust Bank detects, prevents and reports money
laundering and terrorist financing. Money laundering is the process of making illegally obtained money look legal
by moving it through bank accounts and transactions. This policy protects the bank, its customers and the
financial system. Every employee must read it and follow it. 2. The Three Stages of Money Laundering
Money laundering usually happens in three stages. Placement is when illegal cash is first put into the financial
system, for example by depositing cash into an account. Layering is when the money is moved through many
accounts and transactions to hide where it came from. Integration is when the money is used to buy property,
cars or businesses so it looks like legal income. Staff must watch for all three stages, not only for large cash
deposits. 3. AML Reporting Threshold
The AML reporting threshold is a key rule in this policy. Any single cash transaction of SAR 60,000 or more must
be reported to the Compliance Department. Multiple linked cash transactions that together total SAR 60,000 or
more within 7 days must also be reported, even if each single transaction is below the threshold. This is called
structuring when a customer deliberately splits a large amount into smaller deposits to avoid the threshold, and
structuring itself must be reported as suspicious. Cash transactions include cash deposits, cash withdrawals and cash payments at the branch. The threshold
applies to Saudi riyals and to foreign currency of equal value. When a transaction reaches the threshold, the
branch officer must complete the Cash Transaction Report form on the same day and send it to the Compliance
Department. The customer must not be told that a report has been filed. 4. Suspicious Activity Reporting
Some transactions are suspicious even when they are below the threshold. Examples include a customer who
cannot explain where the money came from, a customer who makes many large deposits and then transfers the
money abroad the same day, an account that is suddenly used very differently from its normal pattern, and a
customer who asks the officer not to record a transaction. Any employee who sees suspicious activity must file a
Suspicious Activity Report with the Compliance Officer within 24 hours. The employee must not tell the customer
that a report has been made. This is called no tipping off, and breaking this rule is a serious offence. 5. Customer Due Diligence and Enhanced Due Diligence
Normal customer due diligence is the KYC check described in the KYC Policy. Enhanced due diligence applies to
high-risk customers, politically exposed persons, and customers from high-risk countries. For these customers,
the bank must ask for the source of funds and the source of wealth, obtain senior management approval, and
monitor the account more closely. Enhanced due diligence must be refreshed every six months.
title: Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Policy

content:
6. Sanctions Screening
Every customer name and every payment must be checked against the sanctions lists before a transaction is
completed. If a name matches a sanctioned person or entity, the transaction must be stopped immediately and
the Compliance Officer must be informed. No payment may be released to a sanctioned person under any
circumstances. 7. Training and Awareness
All employees must complete AML training once a year. New employees must complete it within 30 days of
joining. Branch managers must keep a record of who has completed the training. Any employee who is unsure
whether a transaction is suspicious should ask the Compliance Officer — asking is always better than staying
silent. 8. Record Keeping and Penalties
AML records, including transaction reports and suspicious activity reports, must be kept for at least ten years. Failure to follow this policy can lead to disciplinary action, loss of employment, fines for the bank and criminal
prosecution for the employee. The bank has zero tolerance for any employee who helps a customer hide illegal
money. Arabic Summary

content:
SAMA Compliance Summary
Document: SAMA Compliance Summary | Version: 1.0 | Department: Compliance | Effective: January 2026 |
Review: July 2026
1. Purpose
This document summarises, in plain language, the main compliance duties that Riyadh Trust Bank follows under
the rules of the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA). It is a training summary for bank staff. It is not the official SAMA
rulebook and it does not replace the official regulations. Whenever this summary and an official SAMA circular
disagree, the official circular must be followed. Staff who need the full text must ask the Compliance Department. 2. Who is SAMA
The Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) is the central bank of Saudi Arabia. It supervises banks, finance companies and
insurance companies in the Kingdom. SAMA issues licences, sets prudential rules, and checks that banks follow
them. SAMA can inspect a bank at any time, ask for reports, and take action against a bank that breaks the rules. Compliance with SAMA rules is therefore not optional. 3. Key SAMA Requirements
3.1 Licensing and governance
The bank must hold a valid SAMA banking licence and must have a board of directors, an audit committee and a
risk committee. Senior managers must be fit and proper, which means they must have the right experience and a
clean record. Any change in senior management must be reported to SAMA. 3.2 Capital and liquidity
The bank must hold enough capital to absorb losses, as set by SAMA's capital adequacy rules. It must also hold
enough liquid assets to pay customers who withdraw their money. The Finance Department reports capital and
liquidity figures to SAMA every month. 3.3 Customer protection
SAMA's Banking Consumer Protection Principles require the bank to treat customers fairly, to explain products
and fees in clear language before the customer signs, to handle complaints quickly, and to protect customer
data. A customer complaint must be answered within 15 working days. If the customer is not satisfied, they may
complain to SAMA. 3.4 Cyber security framework
Under the SAMA Cyber Security Framework, the bank must protect its systems against cyber attacks, control who
can access sensitive systems, monitor for unusual activity, and report serious cyber incidents to SAMA within the
required time. Staff must not share passwords, must lock their screens, and must report phishing emails to the IT
security team. 3.5 Anti-money laundering
SAMA requires banks to have an anti-money laundering programme, to verify customer identity, to monitor
transactions, and to report suspicious activity. The details are in the bank's AML Policy. SAMA inspectors check
these controls during their visits. 3.6 Reporting to SAMA
The bank must send regular reports to SAMA, including financial statements, large exposure reports, and reports
of fraud. Reports must be accurate and sent on time. Late or wrong reporting is itself a breach of SAMA rules.
title: SAMA Compliance Summary

content:
4. Compliance Calendar
The Compliance Department keeps a calendar of all SAMA reporting deadlines and inspection dates. Branch staff
must send any information the Compliance Department asks for at least five working days before a deadline. Missing a deadline can lead to a fine, so no request from Compliance may be treated as low priority. 5. What Happens if the Bank Breaks the Rules
SAMA can warn the bank, fine the bank, restrict its activities, remove a manager, or in extreme cases withdraw
the licence. Individual employees who deliberately break the rules can also be fined or banned from working in
banking. For this reason, every employee must ask the Compliance Officer whenever they are unsure about a
rule. Arabic Summary

Personal Loan Policy
Document: Personal Loan Policy | Version: 1.0 | Department: Retail Banking | Effective: January 2026 | Review:
January 2027
1. Purpose
This Personal Loan Policy explains who can get a personal loan from Riyadh Trust Bank, how much they can
borrow, what it costs, and how the loan is repaid. It covers personal loans and home loans offered to individual
customers. Business loans are covered by a separate policy. 2. Who Can Apply
To apply for a personal loan, the customer must be at least 21 years old and no older than 60 years at the end of
the loan term. The customer must be a Saudi national or a resident with a valid Iqama and at least one year
remaining on it. The customer must have a salary account with the bank, or must agree to transfer their salary to
the bank before the loan is paid out. The customer must have been employed with the same employer for at
least three months, or self-employed for at least two years with proof of income. 3. Loan Amount and Term
The minimum personal loan is SAR 5,000 and the maximum is SAR 250,000. The maximum amount also depends
on the customer's monthly salary: the total monthly instalment for all loans must not exceed 33 percent of the
customer's monthly salary. The loan term is between 12 months and 60 months. A home loan is larger and
longer and is approved separately under the Home Loan Procedure. 4. Profit Rate and Fees
The bank charges a fixed annual profit rate, which is shown on the loan offer and does not change during the
loan term. The current indicative rate for a personal loan is 5.5 percent per year, but the exact rate depends on
the customer's risk rating and the loan term, and the final rate is always the rate written on the signed offer. There is an administrative fee of 1 percent of the loan amount, with a maximum of SAR 5,000. There is no fee for
early settlement after the first year, but a fee of one month's profit applies if the loan is settled within the first
year. 5. Documents Required
The customer must provide a valid National ID or Iqama, a salary certificate or employment letter dated within
the last 30 days, a bank statement for the last three months if the salary is not already with the bank, and the
completed loan application form. For a home loan, the customer must also provide the property title deed and a
valuation report. 6. Approval Process
The branch officer checks the documents and enters the application into the system. The system checks the
customer's credit history with the Saudi Credit Bureau (SIMAH) and calculates the debt burden ratio. If the ratio is
above 33 percent, the application is declined. If the ratio is acceptable, the application goes to the credit team,
which approves or declines it within three working days. The customer is informed by SMS and by a phone call. No loan may be paid out before the customer signs the loan contract.
title: Personal Loan Policy

content:
7. Repayment and Late Payment
Repayment is by monthly instalment, deducted automatically from the customer's salary account on the same
day each month. If an instalment is late by more than 7 days, a late fee of SAR 50 applies and the credit team is
notified. If three instalments are missed in a row, the loan is treated as in default and the bank may take legal
action. The customer may ask for a rescheduling of the loan once during the loan term, if they can show a
genuine reason such as job loss or medical emergency. 8. Customer Rights
The customer has the right to receive a copy of the loan contract, to know the total cost of the loan before
signing, to complain if they are treated unfairly, and to settle the loan early. The bank must not pressure the
customer to take a loan they do not need. Arabic Summary

content:
Account Opening Policy
Document: Account Opening Policy | Version: 1.0 | Department: Retail Banking | Effective: January 2026 |
Review: January 2027
1. Purpose
This Account Opening Policy explains how a new account is opened at Riyadh Trust Bank, which types of accounts
exist, and what the customer and the branch officer must do at each step. The policy works together with the KYC
Policy, which explains how identity is verified. No account may be opened without a completed KYC check. 2. Types of Accounts
The bank offers three main types of personal accounts. A current account is for daily transactions, salary and
payments, and comes with a debit card and online banking. A savings account earns a small profit on the balance
and is for money the customer wants to keep aside. A fixed deposit account locks the money for a chosen term,
from 3 months to 24 months, and earns a higher profit, but the money cannot be withdrawn early without a
penalty. The customer may hold one account of each type. 3. Documents Needed for Account Opening
What documents are needed for KYC account opening? The customer must bring a valid National ID card for
Saudi nationals, or a valid Iqama for residents, as the identity document. The customer must also bring proof of
address dated within the last three months, such as a utility bill or a national address certificate. For a salary
account, an employment letter or salary certificate is also needed. For a minor's account, the guardian must
bring the minor's birth certificate and their own identity document. All originals must be seen; photocopies alone
are not accepted. 4. Steps to Open an Account
First, the customer fills in the account opening form, either in the branch or online. Second, the branch officer
checks the identity document and the proof of address against the KYC Policy. Third, the officer enters the
customer details into the core banking system and runs the sanctions and watchlist check. Fourth, the customer
signs the account terms and conditions and chooses the account type. Fifth, the account number is created and
the debit card is ordered. The whole process in the branch should take no more than 45 minutes if all documents
are ready. Online applications are reviewed within one working day. 5. Accounts for Minors and Joint Accounts
An account for a minor under 18 years may only be opened by a parent or legal guardian, who operates the
account until the minor turns 18. A joint account may be opened by two people, who must both be present, both
pass the KYC check, and both sign the form. Either holder may operate the joint account unless the form says
both signatures are needed. 6. Account Activation and Cards
The account becomes active as soon as the account number is created, but the debit card is sent to the branch
within five working days. The customer must activate the card at an ATM or through the mobile app with the PIN
sent by SMS. Online banking is activated at the same time, after the customer sets a password and a one-time
code is verified.
title: Account Opening Policy

content:
7. Closing an Account
A customer may close an account at any time by visiting a branch with their identity document. The remaining
balance is paid to the customer after any outstanding fees are deducted. The bank may close an account if it has
had no activity for 12 months and the balance is zero, after sending two written notices to the customer. All
account records are kept for ten years after closure, as required by the KYC Policy. Arabic Summary

HR Leave Policy
Document: HR Leave Policy | Version: 1.0 | Department: Human Resources | Effective: January 2026 | Review:
January 2027
1. Purpose
This HR Leave Policy explains the leave that employees of Riyadh Trust Bank are entitled to, how to request leave,
and who approves it. It applies to all full-time employees. Part-time employees receive leave in proportion to their
working hours. This policy follows the Saudi Labour Law, and if the law gives the employee more leave than this
policy, the law applies. 2. Annual Leave
Every full-time employee is entitled to 30 calendar days of paid annual leave per year, after completing the
probation period of three months. Annual leave is counted in calendar days, including weekends that fall inside
the leave period. Employees may take their leave in one block or in parts, but no single block may be shorter than
five days unless the manager agrees. Leave must be taken within the year it is earned; up to 10 unused days may
be carried to the next year, and any further unused days are lost unless the manager has refused the leave in
writing. 3. How to Request Leave
The employee must submit the leave request through the HR system at least 14 days before the leave starts, and
at least 30 days before for leave longer than 15 days. The request must state the start date, the end date and the
number of days. The direct manager must approve or reject the request within three working days. If the
manager does not reply within three working days, the employee should remind them; silence is not approval. Leave is only confirmed once it is approved in the system. 4. Sick Leave
An employee who is ill is entitled to paid sick leave of up to 30 days per year, on presentation of a medical
certificate from a recognised hospital or clinic. The first 30 days are paid in full, the next 60 days at three quarters
of the salary, and any further sick leave in the same year is unpaid. The employee must inform their manager on
the first day of sickness and must send the medical certificate within three days of returning to work. 5. Other Leave Types
Maternity leave is 10 weeks of paid leave, taken from four weeks before the expected delivery date. Paternity
leave is 3 days of paid leave on the birth of a child. Marriage leave is 5 days of paid leave. Bereavement leave is 5
days of paid leave on the death of a spouse, parent or child, and 3 days for other close relatives. Hajj leave is 10
to 15 days of paid leave once during employment, for employees who have completed two years of service. Emergency leave of up to 3 days may be granted by the manager for urgent family reasons. 6. Public Holidays
The bank is closed on official public holidays announced by the government, including Eid Al-Fitr, Eid Al-Adha and
National Day. If a public holiday falls during an employee's annual leave, that day is not counted as annual leave.
title: HR Leave Policy

content:
7. Unpaid Leave and Abuse
Unpaid leave may be granted by the HR Director for up to 30 days in special cases, and it does not count towards
the annual leave balance. Taking leave without approval is treated as unauthorised absence and may lead to a
salary deduction and disciplinary action. Forging a medical certificate is gross misconduct and leads to dismissal. Arabic Summary

Charges and Fees Schedule
Document: Charges and Fees Schedule | Version: 1.0 | Department: Retail Banking | Effective: January 2026 |
Review: July 2026
1. Purpose
This Charges and Fees Schedule lists the fees that Riyadh Trust Bank charges for its services. All fees are in Saudi
Riyals (SAR) and include VAT where VAT applies. The bank must show this schedule to the customer before the
customer signs for a product, and the schedule on the bank's website is always the current one. If this document
and the website disagree, the website version applies and the customer must be told. 2. Account Fees
Opening a current account or a savings account is free. There is no monthly fee for a current account as long as
the average monthly balance is SAR 1,000 or more. If the average balance falls below SAR 1,000, a monthly fee of
SAR 25 applies. There is no fee for a savings account. A fixed deposit account has no opening fee and no monthly
fee. Closing an account is free. 3. Card Fees
The first debit card is free. A replacement debit card costs SAR 30 if the card is lost or damaged by the customer,
and is free if the card is faulty. A credit card has an annual fee of SAR 250 for the standard card and SAR 500 for
the gold card, waived in the first year. A supplementary credit card costs SAR 100 per year. A PIN replacement at
the branch costs SAR 15. 4. Transfer Fees
Transfers between Riyadh Trust Bank accounts are free. Transfers to another bank inside Saudi Arabia through
SARIE cost SAR 7 for same-day transfer and are free for next-day transfer. International transfers cost SAR 50,
plus any charges of the receiving bank. A transfer that is returned because the details were wrong costs SAR 25. 5. Cash and Cheque Fees
Cash withdrawals from the bank's own ATMs are free. Withdrawals from another bank's ATM in Saudi Arabia cost
SAR 5 per withdrawal after the first four free withdrawals each month. A cheque book of 25 leaves costs SAR 25. A
stopped cheque costs SAR 50. A returned cheque because of insufficient funds costs SAR 100 and is reported to
the credit bureau. 6. Loan and Other Fees
The loan administrative fee is 1 percent of the loan amount, with a maximum of SAR 5,000, as set in the Personal
Loan Policy. A late loan instalment fee is SAR 50 if the payment is more than 7 days late. A copy of a bank
statement costs SAR 10 per page at the branch and is free through online banking. A liability letter or account
certificate costs SAR 50. 7. Changes to Fees
The bank may change these fees with 30 days' notice, published on the website and sent to customers by SMS. No fee may be charged that is not listed in this schedule or in the product terms the customer signed. Any
customer who believes they were charged wrongly may complain, and the complaint must be answered within
15 working days, as required by the SAMA Compliance Summary. Arabic Summary

PDPL Data Privacy Summary
Document: PDPL Data Privacy Summary | Version: 1.0 | Department: Compliance | Effective: January 2026 |
Review: July 2026
1. Purpose
This document summarises, in plain language, how Riyadh Trust Bank protects personal data under the Saudi
Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL). Personal data is any information that identifies a person, such as their
name, National ID number, phone number, address, account number or photograph. This summary is for staff
training. It is not legal advice, and the bank's Data Protection Officer must be consulted for any question about
the law. 2. Principles of Data Protection
The bank follows six principles. First, data is collected only for a clear purpose, such as opening an account or
providing a loan, and is not used for another purpose without consent. Second, only the data that is needed is
collected — no more. Third, data must be accurate and kept up to date. Fourth, data is kept only as long as
needed, and for at least ten years after an account is closed where the KYC Policy requires it. Fifth, data is kept
secure with access controls and encryption. Sixth, the bank is accountable and must be able to show that it
follows these principles. 3. Customer Rights
Under the PDPL, every customer has the right to know what personal data the bank holds about them, to ask for
a copy of it, to ask for it to be corrected if it is wrong, and to ask for it to be deleted when it is no longer needed
and no law requires it to be kept. The customer also has the right to withdraw consent for marketing at any time. The bank must answer a customer data request within 30 days. The customer may complain to the Saudi Data
and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA) if they are not satisfied with the bank's answer. 4. Consent and Sharing
The bank must get the customer's consent before collecting personal data, except where the law requires the
collection, such as KYC identity checks. Personal data must not be shared with any other company without the
customer's consent, except where the law requires it, for example to SAMA, to a court, or to the credit bureau
SIMAH. Data must not be transferred outside Saudi Arabia without the approval of the Data Protection Officer
and the controls required by the PDPL. 5. Data Breaches
A data breach is when personal data is lost, stolen or accessed by someone who should not see it. Any employee
who discovers or suspects a data breach must report it to the Data Protection Officer and the IT security team
immediately, and no later than 24 hours after discovery. The bank must assess the breach, contain it, and notify
SDAIA and the affected customers if the breach is serious, within the time required by the PDPL.
title: PDPL Data Privacy Summary

content:
6. Employee Duties
Employees must only access customer data that they need for their own work. They must not look at the
accounts of family members, friends or colleagues out of curiosity. They must lock their screens when they leave
their desk, must not send customer data to a personal email address, and must not discuss customer
information outside the bank. Every access to customer data is recorded in the audit log. Breaking these rules is
gross misconduct and can lead to dismissal and to a fine under the PDPL. Arabic Summary
